noveltyJustification: The scan found a further runtime aggregator that collapses sub-track documents into the outer track, plus documented recursive discovery that already traverses nested folders.
focus: Q1: complete the inventory of one-level track assumptions and what each does with a sub-track packet today.
answeredQuestions: Q1: Which spec-kit sites (code, hooks, generators, gates, docs) assume a track sits directly under specs/, beyond the seven already known, and what does each do with a packet inside a sub-track today?

label: The shared track-root reader only recognizes spec-less directories immediately under specs/ and only counts numbered immediate children. Refresh and pre-push reuse this reader, while create.sh declines refresh when the track argument contains a slash. A named sub-track therefore has no independent root sweep or create-time metadata refresh.

Recursive validation started at an outer track enumerates numbered direct children and skips a nonnumeric sub-track directory. archive.sh rejects a packet whose parent path contains that named segment, and its track_of helper returns a track only for a packet directly under specs/<track>.

retrofit-convention.mjs defines a track as the first two relative path segments. Its --track prefix filter can select a nested sub-track path, but byTrack planning and write counts still bucket those documents under specs/<outer-track> rather than the named sub-track.

Current documentation illustrates direct track-to-packet paths and phase nesting whose every parent and child name is numeric. It does not define the requested nonnumeric named sub-track segment; this is a documentation and model boundary, not evidence that the generic recursive document scanner rejects nested packets.
